title: Policy Slider Intelligence
description: Turn each policy slider into an educational tool: description, intended effect, likely side effects, uncertainty level, affected score categories and real-world examples, surfaced via progressive disclosure.
rationale: The sliders are the primary interaction. Annotating them turns a black-box calculator into a teaching instrument, increasing trust, engagement and the quality of scenarios users build.
success_criteria: Every slider has all six metadata fields populated
Metadata is accessible in the UI without overwhelming the controls
Affected score categories reference real EPIC-003 categories
Uncertainty levels are explicit and consistently scaled
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Per-slider metadata: description, intended effect, likely side effects, uncertainty level, affected score categories, real-world examples

## Out of scope
- Changing the engine's maths (EPIC-012)
- AI generation of explanations now (future; soft-linked EPIC-008/010)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-001 - sliders/levers and their meanings must exist
- Benefits from EPIC-003 to reference affected score categories

## Assumptions
- Metadata is human-authored, curated and sourced where claims are made
- Real-world examples are illustrative and caveated
- Metadata is data (not code), enabling later AI assistance

## Risks
- Over-confident claims -> explicit uncertainty levels; neutral, sourced wording
- Metadata drifts from engine behaviour -> link to lever ids; validate coverage
- UI clutter -> progressive disclosure (tooltip/expander), not always-on

## Future extensions
- AI-assisted explanations (soft-link EPIC-008/010), clearly labelled
- Inline 'what if I change this?' micro-simulations
- Localisation of slider metadata
